definition: An interpreter directly executes instructions written in a programming or scripting language without previously converting them to an object code or machine code.
details: An interpreter directly executes instructions written in a programming or scripting language without previously converting them to an object code or machine code. A compiler, on the other hand, transforms high-level code into machine code that the computer's processor can execute directly.

explainer.lead: The distinction separates execution approaches: an interpreter directly executes instructions in a programming or scripting language, while a compiler transforms high-level code into machine code the processor executes directly. It matters because the choice shapes how and when code runs.

tiers.eli5: An interpreter is like a live translator speaking as you talk; a compiler is like translating a whole book ahead of time so it can be read directly.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick interpreters for direct execution of scripting languages and compilers for producing machine code ahead of execution. A pitfall is assuming the two are mutually exclusive, when a language implementation can involve both stages.
tiers.paperLevel: An interpreter directly executes instructions without previously converting them to object or machine code; a compiler transforms high-level code into machine code the processor executes directly. Limits: this is a simplified dichotomy, and real implementations often mix both approaches.

explainer.example: A script run line by line by an interpreter versus the same program compiled into machine code before the processor runs it.
